finding:
Source: [SKY001](https://docs.skylit.ai/platform/overview), captured 2026-09-06, full readable text L1–41.

Evidence/claim: Platform overview describes API access as coming soon; the later changelog describes a limited beta. Documentation is not evidence of usable account entitlement.

Disposition and improvement: Unresolved dependency for optional vendor benchmarks; our architecture must run on independently audited acquired data.

Source: [SKY002](https://docs.skylit.ai/platform/support), captured 2026-09-06, full readable text L1–30.

Evidence/claim: Support links and channels provide routes for questions, not algorithmic definitions or evidence of edge.

Disposition and improvement: Reference only; no support messages or account actions were sent.

Source: [SKY003](https://docs.skylit.ai/platform/changelog), captured 2026-09-06, full readable text L1–47.

Evidence/claim: June 29 changelog describes limited beta API access for approved developers. Interfaces and claims require versioned capture.

Disposition and improvement: Retain versioned provenance and verify entitlement before any future paid integration.

Source: [SKY004](https://docs.skylit.ai/introduction), captured 2026-09-06, full readable text L1–116.

Evidence/claim: Gamma/vanna strike boards, large nodes, multi-asset comparison, and changing node magnitude organize discretionary location/context hypotheses. Screenshots do not reveal complete holdings, formulas, fills, or uncertainty.

Disposition and improvement: Retain measurable board states; replace narrative certainty with causal targets and uncertainty-aware node models.

Source: [SKY005](https://docs.skylit.ai/intended-audience), captured 2026-09-06, full readable text L1–25.

Evidence/claim: Product is aimed at active traders interpreting options-related market structure.

Disposition and improvement: Reference only; audience claims do not validate economic suitability for one-mini NQ/ES execution.

Source: [SKY006](https://docs.skylit.ai/core-concepts), captured 2026-09-06, full readable text L1–262.

Evidence/claim: Absolute magnitude and sign interact; large nodes, intervening gatekeepers, clusters, early-session movement versus later pinning, post-touch growth/decay, and migrating ceilings/floors describe candidate states. The page also makes retest-frequency, broker-liquidation-time, OPEX, and margin claims without independently demonstrated estimates. Sparse exposure is not observed order-book liquidity.

Disposition and improvement: Retain node-state hypotheses and mechanically decomposed updates. Reject universal midpoint avoidance or an asserted 1:1 payoff implying no edge. Broker-specific timing remains an unverified event hypothesis; do not identify traders from it.

Source: [SKY007](https://docs.skylit.ai/navigating-skylit-web-app), captured 2026-09-06, full readable text L1–66.

Evidence/claim: Board controls change symbol, metric, expiration, view, and replay context.

Disposition and improvement: Record the exact board universe and settings with every derived observation; display settings cannot define a stable research feature silently.

Source: [SKY008](https://docs.skylit.ai/how-to-read-and-use-heatseeker), captured 2026-09-06, full readable text L1–90.

Evidence/claim: The guide prefers agreement among SPX/SPY/QQQ and describes node proximity and multi-board context.

Disposition and improvement: Replace mandatory agreement with an ablated joint predictor: a source-market reaction may matter to NQ without a local QQQ/NQ node.

Source: [SKY009](https://docs.skylit.ai/best-practices), captured 2026-09-06, full readable text L1–101.

Evidence/claim: Prior movement, remaining room, GEX/VEX structure, source-market floors and stronger nodes elsewhere can alter a local trade interpretation.

Disposition and improvement: Retain competing opportunities, cross-market transmission, and remaining-payoff tests. Do not impose an unsupported payoff-ratio cutoff independent of hit probability and costs.

Source: [SKY010](https://docs.skylit.ai/limitations), captured 2026-09-06, full readable text L1–67.

Evidence/claim: News, liquidity conditions, squeezes, expiration effects, and stale or changing maps can defeat a displayed setup.

Disposition and improvement: Use explicit event/freshness/universe states and failure labels; limitations motivate tests rather than discarding options-derived locations.

Source: [SKY011](https://docs.skylit.ai/common-pitfalls-and-mistakes), captured 2026-09-06, full readable text L1–97.

Evidence/claim: The guide discusses proximity margins, chasing, and behavioral errors.

Disposition and improvement: Treat instrument-dependent margins as benchmarks to calibrate in volatility/tick units; psychological admonitions map to deterministic risk and re-entry controls, not explanatory alpha.

Source: [SKY012](https://docs.skylit.ai/faqs), captured 2026-09-06, full readable text L1–95.

Evidence/claim: Kings, gatekeepers, clusters, and stacked concentrations describe board topology and possible interactions.

Disposition and improvement: Represent topology continuously and retain exceptions; no named pattern is automatically a necessary trade condition.

Source: [SKY013](https://docs.skylit.ai/examples-and-case-studies), captured 2026-09-06, full readable text L1–57.

Evidence/claim: TSLA, SPX/SPY/QQQ, and NFLX examples illustrate downward paths, cross-board rejection, changing node strength, and a later gap. Event and stock-split context may confound the NFLX story.

Disposition and improvement: Case fixtures preserve visible sequences; screenshots and selected successes are not realized-fill or causal evidence.

Source: [SKY014](https://docs.skylit.ai/resources), captured 2026-09-06, full readable text L1–19.

Evidence/claim: External video/channel links are supplied, without all referenced audiovisual contents in the captured pages.

Disposition and improvement: Unreviewed linked videos are explicitly outside the reviewed-text claim; request specific missing proprietary explanation only if a proposed component depends on it.

Source: [SKY015](https://docs.skylit.ai/patternpedia/pattern-the-whipsaw), captured 2026-09-06, full readable text L1–35.

Evidence/claim: Opposing larger nodes with limited intervening structure define the illustrated whipsaw configuration.

Disposition and improvement: Retain topology, reach, alternating-touch, and time-to-resolution hypotheses; estimate conditional outcomes on complete opportunity sets.

Source: [SKY016](https://docs.skylit.ai/patternpedia/pattern-rainbow-road), captured 2026-09-06, full readable text L1–35.

Evidence/claim: Many intermingled substantial nodes create an unclear path in the examples.

Disposition and improvement: Compare uncertainty-based abstention with predictive topology models; do not equate visual complexity with proven unprofitability.

Source: [SKY017](https://docs.skylit.ai/patternpedia/pattern-the-gatekeeper), captured 2026-09-06, full readable text L1–39.

Evidence/claim: A nearer intervening node may react before a farther target. Suggested scaling is incompatible with the primary one-contract experiment.

Disposition and improvement: Preserve nearer-versus-deeper opportunity cost, stopping-time labels, and single-position exit choices; no partial exits in the primary policy.

Source: [SKY018](https://docs.skylit.ai/patternpedia/case-study-speculative-and-decoy-nodes), captured 2026-09-06, full readable text L1–35.

Evidence/claim: Examples compare large distant nodes, nearer intervening levels, prior rallies, and horizon limitations. Intentional decoy positioning is not observable.

Disposition and improvement: Retain reachability and expiry-conditioned opportunity; discard inferred intent as a ground-truth label.

Source: [SKY019](https://docs.skylit.ai/patternpedia/pattern-trend), captured 2026-09-06, full readable text L1–37.

Evidence/claim: Trendward node migration, fading opposing structure, and renewed magnitude at departed nodes frame continuation and possible return.

Disposition and improvement: Separate holdings-assumption changes from spot/IV/time repricing and test migration/return forecasts incrementally.

Source: [SKY020](https://docs.skylit.ai/patternpedia/pattern-rug-setup), captured 2026-09-06, full readable text L1–34.

Evidence/claim: The illustrated sequence combines unwinding overhead structure and missing downside support; another board can provide the source catalyst.

Disposition and improvement: Retain directed source-event features, including SPY-to-QQQ/NQ transmission without a local counterpart; test delays and executable incremental payoff.

Source: [SKY021](https://docs.skylit.ai/patternpedia/the-ten-commandments-of-using-heatseeker), captured 2026-09-06, full readable text L1–20.

Evidence/claim: The page gives categorical reversal and color-based trading instructions.

Disposition and improvement: Benchmark-only rules; reject them as universal eligibility restrictions. Context/Location can independently originate entries.

Source: [SKY022](https://docs.skylit.ai/patternpedia/topping-patterns-bottoming-patterns), captured 2026-09-06, full readable text L1–47.

Evidence/claim: Multi-expiry stair steps, declining higher structures, and changes in lower support are interpreted as topping; renewed higher-node growth can invalidate it.

Disposition and improvement: Retain time-evolving strike-expiry graphs and mirrored hypotheses, with causal invalidation and competing explanations.

Source: [SKY023](https://docs.skylit.ai/help-page/general-information), captured 2026-09-06, full readable text L1–14.

Evidence/claim: General product support and orientation.

Disposition and improvement: Reference only.

Source: [SKY024](https://docs.skylit.ai/help-page/written-guides), captured 2026-09-06, full readable text L1–21.

Evidence/claim: Links return to relevant written documentation already included in this review.

Disposition and improvement: Retain navigational coverage; do not count duplicate guides as independent evidence.

Source: [SKY025](https://docs.skylit.ai/help-page/video-links), captured 2026-09-06, full readable text L1–31.

Evidence/claim: Video links and channels are listed; their unseen content is not equivalent to the page text reviewed here.

Disposition and improvement: Record unavailable audiovisual detail; no invented transcripts or omitted-formula reconstruction.

Source: [SKY026](https://docs.skylit.ai/help-page/useful-threads), captured 2026-09-06, full readable text L1–47.

Evidence/claim: Links lead to community/private discussion threads not accessed in this task.

Disposition and improvement: Unavailable external evidence; design does not depend on private account access.

Source: [SKY032](https://docs.skylit.ai/flowseeker/overview), captured 2026-09-06, full readable text L1–396.

Evidence/claim: Print feed, contract aggregation, ranking, lookup, and bookmarks expose DTE, moneyness, premium, OI, volume/OI, side, sweep, and multi-leg filters. Trade side and print size do not establish intent or new holdings. Off-exchange equity prints are not automatically directional.

Disposition and improvement: Keep print→contract→strike→expiry→chain→sector aggregations in separate units. Log unselected candidates; model side/multi-leg uncertainty; preserve OI reporting delay. Atlas flow-bar height is premium, not contracts.

Source: [SKY085](https://docs.skylit.ai/atlas/overview), captured 2026-09-06, full readable text L1–344.

Evidence/claim: Expiration selection changes the board universe. Orb clamping/opacity changes visual size. Replay is described as historical; derived NQ/ES overlays use selected related boards with undocumented mapping. Flow, dark-print, heatmap, and named layouts combine existing data.

Disposition and improvement: Verify as-of behavior; version visual transformations. Extend Nasdaq comparisons explicitly to NDX/NDXP. Treat overlay mapping and beta projections as unreplicated vendor benchmarks, not formulas inferred from screenshots.

Source: [SKY086](https://docs.skylit.ai/atlas/drawing-presets), captured 2026-09-06, full readable text L1–94.

Evidence/claim: Drawing tools support ratios, reversal/log controls, and mutable presets.

Disposition and improvement: Presentation/reference only unless a precise causal rule is separately specified; version presets used to construct benchmark fixtures.

Source: [SKY087](https://docs.skylit.ai/atlas/indicators/gex-vwap), captured 2026-09-06, full readable text L1–43.

Evidence/claim: Each minute, exposure magnitude weights strikes. Upper/lower averages split around the resulting center, not spot. Node filtering is a fraction of king magnitude, not a percentile. Optional early-session envelopes require enough board minutes; session envelopes widen. Missing boards create gaps.

Disposition and improvement: Specify our transparent magnitude-weighted formula and sign-specific alternatives. Preserve opening-window availability, expiry scope, and mapping uncertainty; do not call this traded-volume VWAP.

Source: [SKY088](https://docs.skylit.ai/atlas/indicators/vwap), captured 2026-09-06, full readable text L1–32.

Evidence/claim: Bar price times volume supports period resets and weighted-deviation or percentage bands. SPXW borrows ES volume, including futures-session effects on larger bars.

Disposition and improvement: Label index proxy weighting explicitly. Compare trade-level futures VWAP with bar approximations; forming bars remain provisional and resets are not price gaps.

Source: [SKY089](https://docs.skylit.ai/atlas/indicators/cvd), captured 2026-09-06, full readable text L1–41.

Evidence/claim: Documentation describes sided-volume accumulation, reset/carry modes, averages, missing-data behavior, and SPXW using ES flow. Minute-based reconstruction can change live intraminute wick appearance.

Disposition and improvement: Minute net volume cannot recover true trade-sequence CVD highs/lows. Preserve user-required trade-level and size-cohort CVD OHLC separately, plus options/gamma variants.

Source: [SKY090](https://docs.skylit.ai/atlas/indicators/volume-profile), captured 2026-09-06, full readable text L1–35.

Evidence/claim: Despite histogram language, the described price allocation spreads bar volume across bar range. Defaults and tie/expansion rules affect POC/value area; empty neighbors may stop expansion before the nominal coverage.

Disposition and improvement: Use actual trade-price and signed trade-price profiles for canonical futures objects. Keep the vendor bar allocation as a labeled approximation, and avoid future-viewport selection.

Source: [SKY091](https://docs.skylit.ai/atlas/indicators/tpo), captured 2026-09-06, full readable text L1–48.

Evidence/claim: Letters represent chart bars visiting price rows, with configurable/repeating windows and adaptive row sizing. Prior naked levels appear at the next session open; display hides distant levels.

Disposition and improvement: Compare fixed-tick, causally anchored TPO with OHLC visitation approximations. Separate object availability at completed formation from delayed display and censoring by viewport.
Limited beta; multi-symbol heatmaps, up to 365-day replay, and live-only velocity. Benchmark horizon and entitlement are explicit dependencies.
Credits meter requests/streams separately from rate ceilings. Any future integration needs a fixed request budget and acquisition approval; no calls made here.

Strike values sum returned expirations; gamma/vanna alternatives; default 92 strikes around spot, maximum 400. No exposed per-expiry board tensor or published exposure-unit convention is established by this endpoint. Preserve asOf and universe truncation.

Nearest snapshot is not necessarily at-or-before requested time; replay omits velocity and returns no_data if absent. Reject future asOf; repeated earlier query does not reconstruct unarchived velocity.

One symbol per SSE connection, full snapshot plus separate velocity updates, reconnect lifecycle and concurrent-stream cap. Snapshot/velocity pairing needs source timestamps, deduplication, and stale-state handling.

Capped recent print feed with directional score, conviction multiplier, optional cluster fields and configurable weights. Completed-bucket freshness is described in shared API text. Compare transparent signed flow and calibrated specialists; capped rows cannot reconstruct total flow.
Arbitrary-window server aggregation avoids the print row cap and exposes counts and directional premium split. Reconcile aggregate to raw rows under identical exclusions and half-open boundaries.
Ticker tide distinguishes bucket and cumulative premium, volume, counts, and bucket start/end. Availability is after bucket completion; cumulative values must not be summed across bars.
Time-of-day mean/SD baseline uses 1–30 trailing trading days, default 20, with per-bucket sample count. Require anchor-relative history, zero-day handling and robust/expiry-conditioned alternatives.

5/30/60-minute flow versus baseline, z-scores, trend and optional as_of. Insufficient baseline is null. Verify replay-relative baseline and calibrate continuous values; no forced trend category agreement.

Top strikes by net/total premium or volume, premium-side shares and top-three concentration. Explicit denominators and untruncated universe are needed; concentration across correlated expiry rows must not double count.

Daily profile versus trailing 20-day distribution and five similar historical days. Intraday comparison to completed-day profiles would leak or mismatch time. Train-only nearest-neighbor retrieval with available prefixes is our alternative.

Sector/industry aggregation and contributors. Version sector membership; a contributor share of signed net premium can be unstable near zero. Compare gross and signed normalization, ETF flow and constituent flow separately.

Advance/decline refers to directional FIR threshold, not price breadth. The documented zero ratio when no decliners is a sentinel. Retain separate price breadth and options breadth with explicit no-denominator status.

Market totals, directional premium and same-time trailing premium RVOL; optional ticker subset changes universe. No historical anchor here implies live capture or independent reconstruction for causal benchmarks.

Market NCP/NPP are side-aware buying-minus-selling; relaxed script-exclusion variants differ. Bucket/cumulative values, multi-leg/deep-ITM toggles, price overlay and gap flags require versioned semantics.

Logical sweeps group same-contract multi-venue activity within one second. Intraday timeframe is documented as presently ignored; full-day extrapolated summary differs from capped returned sweeps. Never use that daily total earlier; grouping does not prove one parent order.

Documented composite = .4 VWF + .35 SDF + .25 FIR; VWF is actually premium-weighted trade score. Optional exponential decay defaults to 30-minute half-life. Compare transparent benchmark with out-of-sample calibrated mixtures; undocumented component details remain unresolved.

Volume/OI buckets produce claimed accumulation and new-position estimates; zero OI yields ratio zero. These do not identify opening/closing flow. Use explicit undefined-ratio masks and next-report OI labels with constrained uncertainty.

Moneyness buckets and premiums produce strategy labels, with deeper-OTM weighting. Preserve continuous forward moneyness/DTE/liquidity inputs; intent labels are inferred hypotheses, not observed positions.

Trade-level sentiment, urgency, confidence and intent derive from trade context/side. Canonical id matters when timestamps collide. Test side validity and calibration; opening_long_call is not a known execution instruction.

Ask/bid/mid shares here count trades, aggression divides aggressive trades by mid trades, and no-BBO joins mid. Capped ratio sentinels differ elsewhere. Keep counts/contracts/premium versions separate and unknown distinct from neutral.
Contract-level version of execution-side ratios; canonical option key encodes ticker, expiry, right and strike×1000. Resolve adjusted contracts through metadata rather than key text alone.
Call/put-aware directional buckets use contract volume and classify ask calls/bid puts as bullish. This is a signed-flow convention, not proof of directional intent or dealer side.
Same directional convention within one contract. Do not combine with chain ratios as independent evidence; maintain lineage and compare aggregation scales.
Active list means traded during the requested date, ranked by full-day premium, capped at 500. It is neither all listed contracts nor a valid morning point-in-time universe.
Prefix search uses date-active universe. Reference-only discovery; independent instrument definitions establish tradable/listed universe.
Here netPremium = gross callPremium − gross putPremium, unlike side-aware tide. call/put ratio returns zero with no puts. Rename semantically; do not join same-named fields blindly.
Trailing five-trading-day form of daily ranking. Window end must precede decision unless a causal partial-current-day form is reconstructed.
Bulk daily stats omit names without activity; lastPrice is date-end trade. Missing may be inactivity, not zero inventory; historical daily values are unavailable intraday.
Single-underlying daily stats share the same availability and missing-activity limitations.
Underlying chart aggregates options activity plus boundary stock price; baseline slots may be absent. Each bar covers [start,end). It is not ordinary underlying-price OHLCV.

Enriched rows mix event/ingestion timestamps, optional later IV, evolving clusters/strategies, daily volume and OI. Whitelist causal fields and retain feature-specific known_at; exclude nextIv at trade time.

Strike distribution combines call/put premium, volume/OI and max-pain estimate. Expiry mixtures alter payoff geometry; max pain is benchmark-only, not a dealer objective or deterministic settlement forecast.
Strike→expiry breakdown retains an essential second dimension lost by summed boards. Use stable contract identities and expiry-specific normalization before cross-expiry pooling.
Expirations list includes those traded that date. Use definitions to include listed but inactive maturities; avoid full-day activity selection at morning decisions.

Date/expiry snapshot uses last prices/IV and can suppress low-volume strikes. No intraday as-of guarantee follows from date. Build surfaces from valid contemporaneous quotes and preserve coverage mask.
Daily history has activity days only. Calendar-complete joins distinguish holiday, inactive and missing feed, and respect next-available daily publication.

Underlying RVOL exposes actual baseline-day count and nullable baseline. Normalize against causally comparable same-time samples, not complete-day hindsight; compare robust shrinkage for sparse histories.
Daily contract ranking has broad filters and a row cap. Retain as a display benchmark; use all eligible point-in-time candidates for model selection and log rejected rows.
Five-day contract ranking inherits daily selection and expiry-aging issues. Do not repeatedly count the same contract as independent evidence.

Unusual-volume scanner defaults to previous calendar day, not previous trading day, and requires baseline volume. Specify date explicitly; sparse/new contracts need a separate model and missing-baseline status.

Unusual-OI opening/closing tags refer to net reported OI change, not individual trade open/close flags. Align report date/publication time and distinguish exercises, expiry, revisions and observed volume.
Bulk contract stats omit inactive contracts. Keep missing activity distinct from missing OI, contract delisting and feed failure.
Single-contract daily stats have the same publication and incompleteness constraints.
Contract bars preserve granular side buckets, single-leg volume, cumulative daily totals, VWAP and IV. Reconcile to raw trades; side sub-buckets and cumulative totals require disjoint aggregation.

Contract-scoped enriched trades offer microsecond timestamp detail absent in some underlying views. Preserve source precision and independent ordering/receipt uncertainty; same timestamp alone is not a unique trade.
Contract daily history combines OI changes, executions, VWAP and IV. Use as future labels or lagged features according to individual publication rules.
Contract RVOL requires expiry-age, listing-age, moneyness and sample-count controls. A ticker-level baseline is an explicit alternative, not interchangeable history for the same contract.

TRF prints have shares/notional and venue but no side/BBO/Greeks. Date-span and offset caps, plus heuristic hasMore, need complete pagination checks. TRF is a reporting channel, not proof of a dark-pool execution.

Largest individual prints over a calendar-day window are candidate anchors; as_of_date includes that whole date. Filter by receipt before a decision and test placebo levels; size is not guaranteed support/resistance.
OpenAPI metadata is a reproducible interface reference, not an additional market signal.
MCP wraps the same REST data and credits, with session/concurrency limits. No new predictive information or independent evidence comes from transport.
Access requires account entitlement; setup instructions were read but not executed. No agent-driven paid market-data queries were initiated.
Catalog advertises 40 tools while overview says 38. This illustrates version drift; discover actual capabilities only in a separately authorized integration, and record schema versions.
Example workflows combine heatmaps and flow, but their wording treats positioning/intent more confidently than the data identifies. Retain joint-feature experiments with measurement uncertainty.
Nexus documentation is coming soon; no substantive algorithm is available. Social-layer dependency deferred and unnecessary for the proposed core.

OHLCV history uses [from,to), bar-open timestamps, sided equity volume where available, and countback precedence. RTH is default; history limits depend on storage tier. Larger bars cannot reconstruct trade-sequence CVD extrema.
Ranked symbol picker is reference metadata; canonical id differs from display ticker. No evidence of complete historical listing universe.
Symbol resolution includes price scale/session/timezone. Validate these against contract records and historical changes rather than relying on current metadata for all history.
Configuration exposes history caps and can be cached while server limits change. Future adapter should version capability snapshots and handle authoritative rejection without blind retries.
Server time measures the vendor clock, not exchange-event or local receipt time. Use for clock diagnostics only.

source: [Corsi, HAR-RV, equation 8 and empirical specification](https://statmath.wu.ac.at/~hauser/LVs/FinEtricsQF/References/Corsi2009JFinEtrics_LMmodelRealizedVola.pdf), pp8,13–14 of PDF
finding: Daily, weekly and monthly realized measures provide an interpretable multiscale statistical challenger. Fit coefficients within each fold; compare variance and log-variance implementations explicitly. Do not copy simulated coefficients or equate backward realized volatility with a forward excursion distribution.

Retain an OHLC estimator that accounts for opening jumps and drift, alongside Garman–Klass. Choice of session close/open matters for nearly continuous futures. Full article access/formula verification remains an implementation reference check, not empirical proof.

source: Garman–Klass original DOI [10.1086/296072](https://doi.org/10.1086/296072); university PDF returned an error and Berkeley preprint fetch failed
finding: Preserve the known OHLC benchmark and independently verify its formula in the implementation fixture. Explicitly record unavailable external full text; do not claim a completed paper review.

Compare realized variance with bipower variation to estimate a jump component under the paper's assumptions. Noise, sparse trading and sampling frequency need robustness checks; the residual is not a perfect event classifier.

Surface fitting must check nonnegative butterfly density and calendar monotonicity of total variance under compatible European-option assumptions. An SVI slice alone is not an arbitrage-free surface. Sparse wings, American exercise and differing settlement times require separate treatment; interpolated wings are estimates, not observations.

Best-quote changes support an OFI measurement with MBP-1. The paper concerns stock data and largely contemporaneous impact; our forecast targets start after feature availability and execution latency. High explanatory fit does not prove future trade profitability. No inference of hidden queues or participant identity.

source: [Jacobs et al., Adaptive Mixtures of Local Experts, original paper](https://www.cs.toronto.edu/~hinton/absps/jjnh91.pdf)
finding: The gating concept motivates target-specific mixtures. Different measurements are not interchangeable experts unless translated to a common target distribution. Specialization, disagreement, calibration, missing experts and out-of-fold downstream training are explicit contracts. Source PDF is scanned; first-page abstract and publication context checked, not a full visual review.

source: [Zaheer et al., Deep Sets](https://arxiv.org/abs/1703.06114), abstract/theorem motivation
finding: Permutation-invariant set encoding is a justified candidate for variable contract/node counts. Preserve strike, expiry, asset and time coordinates as features; arbitrary input order must not change a board forecast. Compare pooled statistics before attention or graphs.

Compare temperature scaling, logistic calibration and isotonic regression on held-out chronological calibration data. The reported image/text results do not guarantee financial calibration. Evaluate reliability by regime and coverage, with intervals and abstention.

source: [Bailey–López de Prado, Deflated Sharpe Ratio](https://www.davidhbailey.com/dhbpapers/deflated-sharpe.pdf), abstract, pp3–8,11
finding: Record every trial, including failures. DSR is a sensitivity diagnostic for selection and non-normality, not a substitute for dependence-aware uncertainty, chronological validation or a truly frozen future period. Correlated trial counts and nonstationarity require sensitivity analysis.

Offline policy evaluation requires support for actions and defensible logging/reward assumptions. No filled-trade history or propensities exist here. We cannot recover passive counterfactual fills or the effect of our unplaced order by applying a DR formula to market replay. Simulation and later shadow/order telemetry remain necessary.

Historical observation date differs from when a value became known. Current-date realtime fields in the acquired series are not historical vintages. Use released-calendar information only where its own availability is defensible; defer revision-sensitive macro values until vintage and intraday publication information are acquired.

Reported OI is a once-daily observation of previous end-of-day stock, generally around 06:30 ET. Actual row/publication availability governs joins. Missing zero-OI reports do not justify interpreting every absent contract as zero. Next-report OI can label an earlier forecast after publication.

Interval quotes are the last quote at the interval timestamp. The default request is RTH; strike_range counts strikes around spot, not dollars. Validate acquisition-version semantics and stale underlying quotes. The sampled snapshot is not proof of full-tape NBBO coverage.

Documented pairing uses quotes no later than the trade; current exclusive default requires a strictly earlier quote. Three sampled archive pairs violate even the non-strict relation. Quarantine/rematch where raw prior quotes exist; otherwise preserve unknown sign. Endpoint documentation alone does not repair acquired records.

On Trade events, B is buyer aggressor and A seller aggressor; other actions can describe the resting side. Keep action-sensitive sign decoding. Native price integers use fixed-point conversion; type-specific sentinel values must become typed missing data before arithmetic.

source: [Parkinson original paper, CME-hosted copy](https://www.cmegroup.com/trading/fx/files/michael_parkinson.pdf), textual sections II–V, journal pp62–64 (PDF pages3–5), including range second moment and log-price substitution
finding: Retain high-low variance `mean(log(H/L)^2)/(4 log 2)` as C23, separate from GK/YZ and from a forward forecast. The paper's diffusion-model efficiency result does not establish modern futures forecast or trading improvement. Test gaps, drift, discrete sampling and same-cohort economic use.

source: [Bollerslev original GARCH paper from the author's university site](https://econ.duke.edu/~boller/Published_Papers/joe_86.pdf), abstract and sections2–3, journal pp309–311/PDF pages3–5, equations1–2/8 and stationarity theorem. Alternative EERI URL returned only a cover; publisher DOI fetch failed.
finding: Retain C24 low-order ARCH/GARCH as a forecast comparator. Positive conditional-variance recursion and persistence constraints are explicit; the paper's inflation example is not NQ/ES evidence. Compare with EWMA/HAR and calibrated tails, and reject unstable fits.
